newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown says wants strong pound.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown says wants strong pound.

text.p: UK opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said he favoured "a strong and competitive pound."
Asked at a news conference if he was comfortable with the present strength of sterling, he replied: "We want a strong and competitive pound."
He added that it was not his practice to comment on daily movements in the currency.

Asked if he believed interest rates should be increased further following the jump in October inflation announced on Thursday, Brown said he had argued after the October 30 rate rise that it had been necessary and inevitable.

"We are now starting to see some of the figures that made it necessary," he said, adding that he would need to see internal Treasury data about the state of the economy before deciding whether a further rate rise is necessary.
Underlying inflation jumped to 3.3 percent year-on-year in October, from 2.9 in September. Last month, base rates were raised by a quarter-point to 6.00 percent.
Brown also said it was essential to tackle the underlying causes of inflation, rooted in a lack of investment.
